title: Protocell formation on micrometeorites
task: Protocell formation by lipid self-assembly on extraterrestrial micrometeorite surfaces
key_results: Lipids autonomously form spherical compartments on micrometeorite surfaces through nanotubes; certain lipid compositions preferentially adhere to micrometeorites vs. natural sand particles
comments: Surface-energy-driven self-assembly is plausible for early-Earth abiogenesis, though the mechanism linking elemental composition to lipid behavior remains mechanistically unclear.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Micrometeorite surface energy drives lipid compartmentalization preferentially over sand
hypotheses.result: Differential lipid behavior observed on micrometeorites vs. sand; elemental composition and surface texture implicated

title: Adaptive low-rank variational quantum algorithm for simulating dissipative dynamics in photosynthetic complexes
task: Quantum simulation of dissipative dynamics in photosynthetic light-harvesting complexes
key_results: Low-rank variational quantum algorithm achieves polynomial scaling O(n^2.5Rd) with mean fidelities 0.87–0.95 for FMO complexes (5–12 chromophores); computational crossover at N=14 chromophores favoring quantum over classical; 3% agreement with experimental energy transfer timescales
comments: Demonstrated NISQ viability on realistic hardware is compelling, though current runtimes (<90 s) apply only to small systems; true quantum advantage requires larger photosynthetic complexes (50–300 chromophores).

hypotheses.hypothesis: Tensor compression and dissipation engineering reduce scaling from O(4^n) to polynomial O(n^2.5Rd)
hypotheses.result: Polynomial scaling achieved; classical exact methods become prohibitive beyond N≈14 chromophores

hypotheses.hypothesis: LR-VQA on NISQ devices maintains high fidelity under realistic noise
hypotheses.result: Fidelity 0.932±0.001 for 7-site FMO complex with IBM Heron noise model

title: Fluorescent probes as markers of cell envelope structure and function in halophilic archaea
task: Evaluate fluorescent probes for cell envelope assessment in halophilic archaea under extreme conditions
key_results: Six fluorescent markers (alamarBlue, resazurin, MitoTracker Orange-CMTMRos, Rhodamine 123, SYTO 9, propidium iodide) tested in Halobacterium salinarum and Haloferax volcanii; propidium iodide showed unreliable behavior with false double-labeling
comments: Systematic probe incompatibility characterization is valuable for extremophile research, but the root causes of propidium iodide failure (high salt, membrane potential) remain unresolved mechanistically.

model_io.model: Fluorescent probe compatibility assay in halophilic archaea
inputs: six fluorescent probes (redox, membrane potential, membrane integrity)
high-salt medium, varied growth phases and metabolic states

hypotheses.hypothesis: Standard fluorescent probes are incompatible with extreme salt and high membrane potential in haloarchaea
hypotheses.result: Propidium iodide unreliable; other probes show growth-phase and timescale dependencies requiring optimization

title: Single-nucleus transcriptomics-based drug screening platform for focal cortical dysplasia
task: Link multicellular disease signatures to therapeutic candidates in focal cortical dysplasia
key_results: Single-nucleus RNA sequencing of 49 FCD specimens identified prominent transcriptional alterations in non-neuronal populations (astrocytes, vascular cells) with endothelial/smooth muscle dysfunction; vascular signatures convergent across FCD subtypes; Connectivity Map integration identified 20 candidates; four compounds (Betamethasone, Lodamin, Valproxam, Licochalcone A) reduced seizure-like activity in vivo
comments: Novel transcriptome-guided drug discovery framework capturing multicellular complexity; vascular dysfunction convergence across subtypes suggests shared pathogenic mechanism, though in vivo efficacy validation in mTOR-driven model awaits full characterization.

model_io.model: Human neocortical FCD specimens (FCDI-III) and mTOR-driven FCD model

hypotheses.hypothesis: Multicellular transcriptional signatures predict effective antiseizure compounds in focal cortical dysplasia
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; identified vascular dysfunction convergence across FCD subtypes; Connectivity Map predicted compounds showed in vivo seizure-suppression activity

title: Inhibiting CXCL12/CXCR4 axis enhances T cell activity in gastric cancer
task: Elucidate CXCL12/CXCR4 axis-mediated immune evasion in gastric cancer
key_results: CXCL12/CXCR4 axis mediates CAF-TAM communication triggering M2 macrophage polarization; CXCR4 silencing reduced M2 macrophages and PD-L1 expression; enhanced T cell proliferation and suppressed tumor growth in vivo; axis acts upstream of PD-L1/PD-1-mediated T cell suppression
comments: Identifies CXCL12/CXCR4 as convergence point for stromal-immune crosstalk in gastric cancer; therapeutic targeting may restore T cell immunity, though combination with PD-1 blockade efficacy needs evaluation.

model_io.model: Murine gastric cancer model with single-cell transcriptomics

hypotheses.hypothesis: CXCL12/CXCR4 axis drives immune evasion by inducing M2 polarization and PD-L1-mediated T cell suppression
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; CXCR4 silencing reduced M2 macrophages and PD-L1 expression with enhanced T cell proliferation and slower tumor growth

title: ENO2 sustains cancer stemness and metastatic competence through a phosphoenolpyruvate-dependent metabolic axis in triple-negative breast cancer
task: Elucidate ENO2-driven metabolic axis sustaining cancer stemness and metastatic competence in TNBC
key_results: ENO2 catalytic activity sustains cancer stem cell properties via phosphoenolpyruvate-dependent axis; ENO2 depletion impairs aerobic glycolysis and oxidative phosphorylation, reduces migration/invasion/CSC frequency, and suppresses metastasis; PEP but not pyruvate rescues CSC traits; PKM2 perturbation partially blunts PEP rescue suggesting additional PKM2-independent mechanisms
comments: Identifies therapeutically actionable metabolic vulnerability in TNBC; demonstrates requirement for ENO2 catalytic activity and reveals complexity of PEP signaling with PKM2-independent effectors.

model_io.model: TNBC cell lines with ENO2 manipulation and orthotopic transplantation

hypotheses.hypothesis: ENO2 catalytic activity sustains cancer stemness through PEP-dependent metabolic axis
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; catalytically competent ENO2 required for CSC maintenance; exogenous PEP restores CSC traits; PKM2 partially mediates but additional PEP-responsive mechanisms exist

title: Intrinsic polyunsaturated fatty acid synthesis capacity dictates ferroptosis sensitivity under restricted arachidonic acid availability
task: Define PUFA biosynthetic capacity as ferroptosis sensitivity determinant under AA-limited conditions
key_results: Ferroptosis sensitivity under AA-restricted conditions dictated by endogenous PUFA synthesis capacity; H1299 cells (impaired FADS2/ELOVL5) require exogenous AA while A549 cells maintain sensitivity via intrinsic synthesis; FADS2/ELOVL5 inhibition phenocopies AA-dependent ferroptosis resistance
comments: Reveals critical metabolic determinant of ferroptosis sensitivity with implications for cancer therapy; physiological lipid availability conditions may explain variable ferroptosis response in tumors.

model_io.model: Human lung adenocarcinoma cell lines (H1299, A549) with lipidomic tracing

hypotheses.hypothesis: Endogenous PUFA biosynthetic capacity determines ferroptosis susceptibility under AA-limited conditions
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; KEAP1-mutant A549 cells retained ferroptosis sensitivity via PUFA synthesis while KEAP1-WT H1299 cells lost sensitivity under AA restriction; genetic/pharmacological synthesis inhibition phenocopied loss

title: Colorectal cancer co-opts an epidermal wound healing program during metastasis to generate disseminated tumor cells
task: Identify cellular states enabling colorectal cancer metastatic dissemination
key_results: Disseminated tumor cells transiently adopt wound-healing program expressing KRT17 with reduced EZH2 activity and activated YAP signaling; state is reversible upon distant organ colonization
comments: Novel lineage plasticity mechanism linking epithelial development programs to cancer dissemination; KRT17+ state represents potentially targetable therapeutic window despite transience.

model_io.model: Patient-derived CRC organoid serial orthotopic transplantation

hypotheses.hypothesis: CRC cells adopt wound-healing program during metastatic dissemination
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; DTCs express wound-inducible keratins including KRT17 before outgrowth, with associated EZH2 downregulation and YAP activation

title: Simulated microgravity with physiological shear reveals endothelial disruption in a dual-stimulus bioreactor
task: Model acute endothelial dysfunction under combined microgravity and shear stress
key_results: Dual-stimulus (simulated microgravity + 3 dyn/cm² shear) induces cytoskeletal disorganization, VE-cadherin junction loss, and altered angiogenic factor secretion (Angpt-2, VEGF, PDGF) in HUVECs after 16 h
comments: Physiologically relevant integration of two independent mechanical perturbations; results highlight synergistic vascular disruption beyond single-stimulus models, though mechanism of interaction remains underexplored.

model_io.model: HUVEC bioreactor with simulated microgravity and laminar shear

hypotheses.hypothesis: Combined microgravity and physiological shear induces acute endothelial dysfunction
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; dual-stimulus caused cytoskeletal disruption and angiogenic factor alterations within 16 h

title: Comprehensive analysis of miRNA expression, secretion profile, and functional network during myogenesis in response to spaceflight
task: Characterize muscle-derived miRNA regulation during spaceflight-induced myogenesis alteration
key_results: Comprehensive miRNA profiling during mouse myoblast myogenesis under spaceflight identified deregulated miRNAs with altered expression and secretion patterns; qRT-PCR validation in disuse-atrophy model confirmed relevance; functional assays demonstrated miRNA roles in target gene expression and myoblast proliferation/differentiation; spaceflight modulates miRNA secretion via RNA-binding proteins
comments: Systems-level miRNA analysis bridging spaceflight physiology to disease mechanism; identifies muscle-derived secreted miRNAs as potential biomarkers and systemic effectors, though specific miRNA targets and RBP regulation require further characterization.

model_io.model: Mouse myoblast myogenesis under spaceflight and disuse-atrophy model

hypotheses.hypothesis: Spaceflight deregulates muscle-derived miRNAs affecting myoblast function and systemic adaptation
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; identified specific miRNA deregulation patterns during myogenesis; spaceflight modulates miRNA secretion via RNA-binding proteins; secreted miRNAs implicated in systemic adaptation

title: GATA1 silencing restrains granulosa cell ferroptosis through downregulation of TFRC in polycystic ovary syndrome
task: Identify GATA1-TFRC axis driving granulosa cell ferroptosis in polycystic ovary syndrome
key_results: GATA1 overexpression in PCOS promotes granulosa cell ferroptosis via TFRC transcriptional activation; GATA1 knockdown increases lipid ROS, malondialdehyde, and iron while reducing glutathione; ferroptosis inhibitor Ferrostatin-1 mitigates GATA1 effects; TFRC overexpression counteracts GATA1 knockdown protection against ferroptosis
comments: Mechanistically links transcriptional control to ferroptotic cell death in reproductive pathology; GATA1 represents potential therapeutic target though PCOS involves complex hormonal context.

model_io.model: PCOS mouse model (DHEA-induced) and KGN granulosa cells

hypotheses.hypothesis: GATA1 promotes granulosa cell ferroptosis via TFRC transcriptional activation in PCOS
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; GATA1 directly binds TFRC promoter to enhance transcription; TFRC overexpression counteracts GATA1 knockdown's ferroptosis protection

title: Extracellular vesicles from inflammatory-primed stromal cells reduce in vitro inflammation in Sandhoff disease model
task: Develop anti-inflammatory MSC-EV adjunct for lysosomal storage disease neuroinflammation
key_results: Inflammatory-primed MSC-EVs (IFEVs) reduced Sandhoff disease neuroinflammation in vitro: decreased IL-6, TNF-α, IL-1β with downregulated NF-κB/p65 and NLRP3; increased Treg proportion and Treg/T-effector ratio in peripheral blood mononuclear cells without cytotoxicity
comments: Demonstrates immunomodulatory potential of primed MSC-EVs as acellular therapeutic adjunct; in vitro feline model results promising but require preclinical in vivo validation.

model_io.model: Feline Sandhoff disease model with inflammatory-primed MSC-EVs

hypotheses.hypothesis: IFEVs reduce neuroinflammation in Sandhoff disease by altering immune cell composition and cytokine profiles
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; IFEVs decreased pro-inflammatory cytokines with NF-κB/NLRP3 downregulation and increased Treg proportion without inducing cytotoxicity

title: ATP6AP2 in osteoblasts couples cortical bone matrix remodeling to osteocyte maturation via MMP14 activation in mice
task: Elucidate ATP6AP2 role in osteocyte differentiation and cortical bone organization
key_results: Osteoblast-lineage ATP6AP2 deletion causes impaired osteocyte maturation, irregular woven bone accumulation, and abnormal osteocyte distribution; ATP6AP2 promotes MMP14 surface localization to drive woven-to-lamellar transition
comments: Identifies previously unrecognized ATP6AP2-MMP14 axis controlling bone remodeling; mechanism specifically involves MMP14 localization rather than expression, suggesting post-translational regulation importance.

model_io.model: Male mice with osteoblast-lineage Atp6ap2 deletion (Atp6ap2OCN-Cre)

hypotheses.hypothesis: ATP6AP2 regulates osteocyte maturation through MMP14 surface localization
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; ATP6AP2 interacts with MMP14 and promotes surface localization; MMP14 expression restores osteocyte development in ATP6AP2-deficient cells

title: Oxidative base damage to telomeres sensitizes cancer cells to ATR inhibition
task: Enhance ATR inhibitor efficacy in cancer via telomeric oxidative damage
key_results: ATR inhibition after 8-oxo-guanine induction reduces cancer cell viability at markedly lower doses than non-cancerous cells; mechanism involves insufficient RPA forcing S-phase progression with unrepaired telomere damage
comments: Clever exploitation of cancer's G1/S checkpoint deficiency to sensitize G2/M dependency, though clinical translation requires controlling oxidative damage induction specificity.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Telomeric oxidative damage combined with ATR inhibition will preferentially kill cancer cells over normal cells
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; cancer cells showed reduced viability at lower inhibitor doses with mechanism involving RPA depletion and forced S-phase progression

comments: Integration of routine hemogram with clinicopathologic data is practical and scalable; SHAP interpretability is valuable for clinical adoption, though external validation across healthcare systems is needed.

title: Specimen quality shapes the actionable genomic landscape in comprehensive cancer genomic profiling

comments: QC-aware CGP selection is pragmatic; finding that specimen quality directly affects actionability of genomic findings has important implications for precision oncology workflows and explains part of the gap between genomic discovery and clinical benefit.

model_io.model: QC-aware variant detection and ML prediction model

hypotheses.hypothesis: Specimen quality affects detection reliability of genomic alterations
